doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: Mary working at the Royal Garden with Joe Oliver's band
summary: Mary explains that she went to the Royal Garden after her daughter was born. Entertainers worked the floor and tables with a chorus while the elevated band played, as in a nightclub with dancing.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You appeared at the Royal Garden too?

Yes, over on Carys Grove. She did. See, I at that time, this was a little later, say a couple of years, we went back down south and come back to Chicago, worked our way down and back again. We played the Grand Theater which was owned by Mr. Miller, the man that owned these monograms. He sent her to the Royal Garden.

Well, I was here for my little girl to be born, you know. She was four weeks old, that's when I went. Before I went back, I went down in Texas to take her down there for Mac to see her. But that's when I worked at the Lincoln, at the Royal Garden.
Were you sort of like the band vocalist that they have now or was it a special act? I never did know much about the Royal Garden. I never got to go there when it was open.

No, you didn't have a vocal like that. The performers would entertain in the center of the floor. And Joe Oliver and them would play. Was that more like a nightclub or a dance hall? Yes, like a nightclub. I didn't know if it was a dance. And dance hall. People did dance too. Yes, yes. You entertained on the floor. I see.

Yes, you entertained on the floor instead of going up there to sing through the mic like the entertainers do now. You'd go around to the tables and then your dancer, the chorus would come out in the center of the floor and dance. And it was our chorus from the show.
I see. I always wondered about the Royal Garden if it was just a dance hall where you pay admission or go in and buy drinks or what it was like. No, no.
It was that entertainment. But a flow show and dancing.
